observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South is a squat armoured quadruped seen head-on: a broad frowning face with a hooked beak-like snout, two small brow horns and a small central horn, under a stack of brown stone-like plates. East is a long, low side profile with the head raised: a rhino-like face, small horns at the brow and two to three overlapping brown plates along the back. observed.south.png: A front view with the face toward the camera: heavy brow, amber eyes, a downturned beak-like snout and a frowning mouth. A crown of small conical horns sits on a plate shield. Brown stone-textured plates with round pits and orange lichen flecks are stacked above the head and over the shoulders. Wrinkled elephant-like legs with rounded toes. The broad south cheek surfaces, rounded leg folds and smoothly bevelled armour in all three facings have continuous sculpt-like shading and uniform fine surface texture. Together they read as a rendered sculpt rather than painted sprite surfaces.

The south face has small recessed eyes, subdued highlights, irregular textured skin and a closed heavy muzzle. Its brow and downturned mouth look stern, but there are no oversized glossy eyes, smiling features or simplified cel-shaded forms establishing a cute or cartoon face.

East shows the head projecting below the high back plates, with its muzzle above the ground in a standing pose. The description identifies grazing behaviour without requiring every sprite to depict active feeding. The tiered, ricochet-pocked armour remains plainly visible; the resting head position alone does not establish a missing defining feature.

edits.change: The calf is a juvenile of the excretor's own alien body plan. A bony face-shield begins to form across the brow and snout. Crusted mineral plates start along the spine and shoulders. Small orange gland nodules sit along the flanks. The hide is grey-blue. The head, ears and hide folds follow this body plan, not a familiar horned animal. The prompt names no Earth animal.

The calf wears the adult's palette: grey-blue skin, pale crusted mineral plates, and orange flank glands. It carries budding versions of the adult's horn layout: one central nasal horn and two curved lateral horns, all short and young. The hide is grey-blue throughout. The brown hide and teal banding are replaced.

Placed beside the adult, the calf reads as the same species. It keeps the adult's palette, plates, flank glands and three-horn layout, at a softer, smaller, juvenile scale. It has a larger head, shorter legs and rounded features.

Front, side and rear views are drawn at one shared scale. The shoulder height and the top of the back sit at the same height in all three views. Body bulk is the same in all three: the side view shows the full barrel body at the same height as the front and rear views.
reference: none. The old render is not used as the reference image. The body is built from the description and the three-horn departure.

pale crusted mineral plates, small and sparse on the spine and shoulders
small orange gland nodules along the flanks
heavy-set, low-slung grazer body with thick pillar legs and a broad blunt browsing muzzle

request.prompt: A young excretor calf: a juvenile of an alien, heavy-set, three-horned grazer that browses ruined ground and concentrates metals and salts in its body. Show three standing views of the same calf at one shared scale, on a transparent background: a front view with the eyes toward the viewer, a side view with the head toward the right of the image, and a rear view seen from behind with the face hidden. All three views stand on the same ground line, with the shoulder and the top of the back at the same height. The body has the same bulk and volume in each view. The side view shows the full barrel body at the same height as the front and rear views. The hide is grey-blue, the same as the adult excretor. A bony face-shield begins to form across the brow and snout. Short pale crusted mineral plates start along the spine and shoulders, overlapping in a small, sparse pattern. Small orange gland nodules sit in a row along each flank. The head carries three budding horns: a short central nasal horn and two short lateral horns that curve outward from the sides of the head. The body is low-slung and heavy-set, with thick pillar legs and a broad, blunt muzzle for browsing along the ground. The ears are small and tucked behind the face-shield. Juvenile proportions: a large head, shorter legs, a rounded belly, softer and smaller plates and horns than the adult. The same grey-blue, plates, orange flank glands and three-horn layout read as the adult's species at calf size. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, with soft painted edges. Value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. All three show the same heavy four-legged animal with thick pillar legs and a layered, plated hide. Three mushroom-like parasol caps rise from the back on rooted stalks. The colouring differs sharply between facings. South: grey-green hide with bold dark tiger-like blotches on the body and legs, and tan caps striped with dark brown. East: brown hide with olive-green moss-like patches on the back plates, brown legs and reddish-pink caps. North: brown and olive hide with plain brown caps. The south looks like a different colour morph from the east and the north.
observed.south.png: A front view. A broad, low head with a beaked, shell-like snout and small eyes faces the camera. The body and legs are grey-green with heavy dark irregular stripes and blotches. Behind the head are a small front cap and a large cap, and the top of a third cap shows above them; all are tan with dark radial stripes, and their gills show underneath. The cut-out is clean, with no ground.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. The body is long and barrel-shaped, with overlapping leathery plates on the back and four thick legs with broad padded feet. The head is low with a hooked, beak-like snout, and a short tail shows at the left. Three parasol caps on root-like stalks rise from the shoulders, mid-back and hips; the middle cap is the largest. The caps are reddish-pink with green-grey on top. The hide is brown, with olive-green mottling on the back plates. No stripes appear. The cut-out is clean.
observed.north.png: A rear view: the haunches, a short pointed tail stub and the backs of four thick legs. No face and no eyes. The large cap and a small rear cap sit on the back, with the front cap's top visible. The caps are plain brown with a little olive, and the hide is brown-olive. No dark stripes appear. The cut-out is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the east facing spans about 3.5 cells and stands roughly 2.5 cells tall, much larger than the human. At 32 px per cell it reads clearly as a big plated beast with three mushroom parasols, well apart from the tan ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult gennok: the same anatomy, pose, three-cap layout and silhouette on all facings. The hide is a uniform warm brown with reddish-pink caps on every facing. The candidate's east facing is very close to this adult's colouring; only its south is a clearly distinct morph.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the haunches, a tail stub and the backs of the legs, with no face and no eyes.

SIGNATURE.seen: Broad parasol-shaped growths on rooted stalks rise from the back on every facing and are clear at both zooms.

ALIEN.seen: The body is rhino- or tortoise-like, but the fungal parasol canopy, beaked snout and layered plates make it read as an alien creature, not a recoloured rhino.

DEPARTURES.seen: The departure 'broad parasol-shaped growths rising from its back' is present: three caps on east, and the large and small caps on south and north.

STYLE.seen: The painting is painterly and realistic, with textured hide, gill detail on the caps and no outlines. It is not cute and not cel-shaded.

request.prompt: A young ivvol, a small flat bottom-dwelling creature for a RimWorld top-down sprite, drawn as a smaller, slightly thicker version of the adult ivvol. The body is a flat, legless, doormat-low disc of maroon-red tissue with a tan wavy rim and fine radiating veins across the mantle, lying flat against the floor. A single raised dorsal ridge runs along the centre of the back, and it carries a short row of proportionally large yellow-orange eyes; this ridge is the only part that stands above the flat mantle, and the eyes along it are the only eyes on the body. The mantle is one unbroken pad of tissue: its edge is a smooth, limbless rim that rests on the ground, and the head, face and limbs are absent, so the whole animal reads as a living floor-mat that watches. Seen from above at a slight angle, with the ridge of eyes turned toward the viewer in the front view, the ridge seen end-on in the side view, and the plain mantle and ridge seen from behind in the rear view. Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast between the maroon mantle, tan rim and yellow-orange eyes carry the silhouette. Small creature, drawn at a size of about 0.8 tiles across.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. Each facing shows a huge domed creature with overlapping armour plates, many thick columnar legs with hoof-like pads, and teal glowing seams between the plates. The plates are coloured differently on each facing. South: grey and rust-red mottling. East: dark slate-blue and violet with ochre/tan mottling. North: mauve-purple and brown with tan mottling. The anatomy and silhouette match from facing to facing.
observed.south.png: A front view with the head toward the camera. A blunt head sits under a pointed front plate. The head has four small glowing yellow-orange eyes in a row and pale curved fang-like mandibles hanging down. Wide domed carapace of overlapping plates. About eight legs spread to both sides. Plate colour is grey with rust-red patches. Clean alpha with no ground.
observed.east.png: A true side profile with the head at the right. A long domed arch of about eight overlapping plates. The head is blunt with a hooked mandible and two glowing yellow eyes visible from the side. At least five legs show on the near side. Plates are dark blue-violet with ochre mottling, legs dark grey. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: A rear view built from tiered, scalloped plates stacked like a stepped dome. No head, no eyes. About ten leg pads show at the base, with a brown fleshy underbody between them. Plates are purple-brown with tan mottling. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is several cells long and about twice the human's height. One plate is roughly a cell or more long. At normal play (32 px/cell) it reads as a large dark domed bug-like mass with legs and a yellow eye glint, clearly apart from the tan ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult: south, east and north with the same anatomy, pose and silhouette as the candidate. Plates are glossy blood-red with blue-dark edges and teal seams, legs dark grey. The adult's colour is the same on all three facings.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows tiered rear plates and leg pads. No head or eyes.

request.prompt: A huge, slow, many-legged grazer for RimWorld, the moravatha in its variant colouring. Body plan: a blunt head carrying four glowing yellow eyes, many legs under a high domed carapace built of overlapping separate plates, each plate as long as a cart; the plates overlap like roof tiles and are not a fused shell. The head and the legs are dull dark grey-violet hide. Colouring, identical on every view: every carapace plate is deep slate-violet (dark blue-purple, low value) with warm ochre mottling in small irregular patches along the plate centres. The hue, value and mottling pattern are the same on the front view, the side view and the rear view. This violet-and-ochre look is clearly different from the adult's blood-red. Surface: glossy, dark and saturated on every view, with a wet-looking sheen, bright specular highlights along the curved ridge of each plate and deep violet shadows in the gaps between plates. The front plates are as glossy and dark as the side and rear plates. Views: the front view shows the blunt face with all four yellow eyes toward the viewer; the side view shows the profile with the full row of legs and the plate dome; the rear view is seen from behind and shows the carapace, plates and rear legs with the eyes hidden. Keep the adult's exact anatomy, proportions and silhouette on every view and change only the plate colouring. Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.

observed.south.png: A head-on blob-like face: a broad dome narrowing upward to a knobbly crest, a large open round mouth with thick pale lips, and tiny pinprick eyes at the corners of the mouth. Iridescent purple/teal skin with skin folds around the mouth. Clean alpha.

observed.north.png: A rear view: an oval body seen end-on and receding, built of stacked ring-like segments that narrow toward the bottom, like a grub or larva. No face, no eyes, no fins, no clear tail fin. Iridescent skin. Clean alpha.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. Each facing shows about 12–13 pointed, lozenge-shaped bodies joined by a branching, glowing yellow-gold thread into a loose net. South: the bodies are dull brown-mauve with mottled pink-purple centres, and their points face up and down. East: the bodies are longer seed or lozenge shapes, olive-gold with dark brown streaks like tiger stripes, and their points face left and right. North: the bodies are pale lavender, blue-grey and purple with soft marbling, and their points face mostly sideways. The net layout and the thread match from view to view, but the colouring of the bodies is clearly different on each facing.
observed.south.png: South at full resolution: 12 lozenges, brown with a pinkish-purple mottled middle. Each lozenge has a small yellow glow at its tip where the thread joins it. A bright yellow web connects them in a roughly hexagonal net. Clean alpha, nothing under the bodies.
observed.east.png: East at full resolution: about 13 tapered lozenges, olive-khaki with dark brown bands running lengthwise, a yellowish sheen, and pointed tips at both ends. The same glowing yellow net joins them and ends in a point on the right. The colouring reads as a different paint scheme from south. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: North at full resolution: about 13 lozenges, pale lavender, grey-blue and violet with white marbling, shaped like plump teardrops. The same glowing yellow net joins them. The colouring is much cooler and paler than south or east. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the net covers roughly the lower half of one cell, much smaller than the human. At 32 px per cell it is a small yellow-and-brown cluster: the yellow thread reads as a tangle and the bodies are small dark specks.
observed.siblings.png: Owner-kept adult shoal: pale cream and translucent lozenges with pink centres on a glowing yellow net. Its south, east and north match the candidate's layout and body count, and its colouring is the same on all three facings.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the net with its lozenge tips pointing toward and away from the viewer. This is the same front layout as the sibling's south.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows no faces or eyes. The bodies are plain marbled lozenges, matching the sibling's north.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: The net is laid out the same way as the owner-kept sibling. No facing is a rotated copy of another facing.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured height spread is 3%, and the three panels look the same size.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The anatomy and net match, but the body colouring changes on each facing: brown-mauve on south, olive with dark stripes on east, pale lavender-blue on north. The variant has no single consistent colouring.

SIGNATURE.seen: The glowing yellow thread linking every body into one net is bright and easy to read on all facings.

ALIEN.seen: A stranger would not name this as a fish or a school of fish. It reads as linked seed pods or lozenges on a glowing web.

DEPARTURES.seen: Line 1: the bodies are lozenges, not fish. They are darker than 'pale', which the owner note allows for a colour variant. Line 2: one glowing yellow thread joins every body, present. Line 3: 12–13 bodies, within eight to fifteen, present. Line 4: the bodies form a connected loose net, not a free school, present.

STYLE.seen: Painterly shading, marbled texture and soft glow on the thread. No heavy keyline, not cute, not a photo.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art matching the sibling's layout. Not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on the checkerboard on all facings. No water, halo or shadow.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The note asks for one distinct colouring of the same species. The anatomy, pose, size and silhouette match the sibling, but the colouring is not one colouring: each facing has a different palette, so the variant does not read as one consistent look.

SCALE.seen: The net is small beside the human, consistent with drawSize 0.7 and with small bodies.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px the yellow net reads as a bright lattice apart from the brown ground. The bodies are small but visible.

North view: rear view, seen from behind, the same brown-mauve mottled lozenges and the same glowing yellow thread, lit from the same side as south and east. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette: the dark brown-mauve bodies and bright yellow thread stand out clearly. Compact framing so the whole net fits a small square sprite, with a little empty space around it.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. observed.south.png: Front view, face toward the camera. A broad violet head with large rounded ears, two small budding horn nubs on the brow, dark eyes and a muzzle lowered slightly toward the viewer. Behind the head is a very wide, rounded violet torso with two lime-green bands that run lengthwise over the top of the back. Thick tan-brown legs with cloven hooves. observed.east.png: True side profile looking right. A slim, fawn-like young grazer on thin tan legs, mid-stride. The neck is carried forward and the head is lowered to the ground in a grazing pose. Soft painterly fur, no outline, clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: haunches, a tufted tail hanging down the middle and tan hind legs. Ears and horn nubs show at the top, seen from behind. There is no face and no eyes. observed.scale.png: At max zoom the east profile stands beside the vanilla human. It is a little shorter than the human and about a cell and a half long, reasonable for a young grazer. At normal play (32 px/cell) it reads as a small striped violet shape, legible against the ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult sulleth: a lean, very long-legged, long-necked grazer with a sleek violet hide, a pale belly, lime-green tiger-like bars on the flanks, olive-green lower legs and a thin dark outline. request.prompt:
A single wild bloodletter petrel for RimWorld, drawn as a walking sea-bird of polluted wastelands, standing on both feet. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic feather texture, soft painted edges, value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Transparent background, one creature centred in the frame, 1.2 tiles wide.

Body: a compact, stout petrel with a rounded chest, long folded wings resting along the back, a short wedge tail and short strong pinkish-grey legs with webbed feet. The beak is a slender, sharply hooked tube-nosed bill in dark horn, its tip stained blood-red, built for piercing prey and drinking blood. The eye is small, dark and alert.

Colouring, identical on every facing: the crown, nape, back, wings and tail are deep charcoal-grey with fine paler feather edges. The face, throat and breast are pale cream. The belly is a lighter cream-grey. The same charcoal cap over the crown and nape sits above the same cream face in every view, and the cream-to-charcoal boundary falls at the eye line.

Front view, eyes toward the viewer: the charcoal crown above the cream face, cream throat and cream breast, with charcoal wing edges at both sides and the red-tipped beak pointing at the viewer.
Side view, seen in profile: the charcoal crown and nape, the cream face patch around the eye and beak base, the cream breast edge, and the charcoal back, wing and tail running to the rear.
Rear view, seen from behind: the charcoal crown, nape, back, folded wings and tail, with a thin cream edge of belly showing at the flanks, and the eyes and beak hidden.

The same bird, the same plumage and the same palette in every view; only the angle changes.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South is a front-on flying insectoid: a small head with a teal dome and two short pale horns or antennae, a slender upright neck and body, two pairs of long olive-yellow veined wings spread out, about six long dark jointed legs hanging down with hooked claws, and a segmented tail hanging below that ends in a large orange feathered fan. East is a side profile looking right: the head with the teal cap and a short snout, an S-curved neck, four wings swept back, legs hanging below, and the long banded tail trailing left to the orange plume fan. North shows the dorsal side: the teal cap seen from behind, no face, the back of the body with stripes, the wings spread, the legs and the tail fan below. The body is a saturated rust-orange with dark tiger-like transverse banding. The plumes are deep orange with dark bases.
observed.south.png: The front view at full resolution. The teal cap sits over a small face, and the snout and face point at the camera. There is a pale cream chest or underside, a rust body with dark banding, olive-green translucent veined wings with darker edges, and dark clawed legs. A blue-grey band on the tail sits above the orange fan. The alpha is clean.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. The head has the teal cap, short pale horns and a pointed snout. The neck and body are rust with dark mottling, and the belly is paler. Four wing layers are swept back, yellow-green and veined. Six long jointed dark legs end in hooked claws. The tail is long and slender, banded blue-grey then rust, and ends in a spreading orange plume fan. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: The rear view. The teal dome is seen from behind with the horn tips at its sides, and no eyes or face are visible. The dorsal neck and body show transverse dark-and-orange banding. The wings are spread and are paler yellow-green than on south. Legs hang to both sides. The tail runs down to a blue-grey band and an orange plume fan. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature spans about 2 cells, wings to tail tip, beside a 1-cell human, so it is clearly much larger than the human. At 32 px per cell it reads as a winged shape with a bright orange tail fan, distinct from the ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult can-cell. The anatomy, pose, silhouette and canvas size match the candidate. The adult is a duller red-brown with a paler underside, has a pale cream-to-peach plume fan, and has less banding on the body.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the teal-capped head with a face and snout toward the camera, the pale chest, and the wings spread to both sides.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the teal dome and a striped dorsal neck and body. No eyes or face are visible.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: South and north are front and rear elevations of a hovering body and east is a side profile. None of the three is a rotated top-down view, and the layout matches the owner-kept siblings.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 13%, within 15%. The facings look the same size on the shared-scale panel.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The teal cap, horns, four wings, clawed legs, banded tail and plume fan are present on every facing and turn with the body. The palette is consistent across facings.

SIGNATURE.seen: The long narrow dragonfly wings, the teal head cap and the large orange plume fan on the tail are all clearly legible.

ALIEN.seen: This is a canon (RSW_) subject, and the card has a section 'Canon — Must show'.

CANON.seen: Present: the large flying insect with a small head on a long upright neck, four long veined translucent wings, several long jointed legs with hooked claws, a long segmented tail with a blue-grey band, the orange plume fan, the teal domed cap with a snout under it, and the realistic painterly rendering. It is not the Clone Wars design and not a plain dragonfly. The colours are shifted for the variant, which the owner note allows.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic: veined membrane wings, textured chitin and soft lighting, no outlines and no cute features.

OURS.seen: This is new art made for the variant commission. Its distinct banded orange palette differs from the sibling, and it is not a retint of donor art.

ALPHA.seen: The checkerboard shows through cleanly around every facing. There is no ground, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The anatomy, pose, size and silhouette match the adult sibling. The colouring is distinct: saturated orange with dark tiger banding, a deeper orange fan and more olive wings, against the adult's dull red-brown and pale peach fan. Only the standing stills are judged.

SCALE.seen: About 2 cells long beside a 1-cell human, which fits 'over 3 m long'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the creature reads as a winged body with a bright orange fan, contrasting with the brown ground.

proposals: The colour variant is distinguishable from the adult mainly by its saturation and banding. A stronger hue shift on the wings or the body could make the variant easier to tell apart at 32 px in a herd.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on one shared scale. South is a squat, rounded creature seen head-on: a broad crocodile-like snout, two yellow slit-pupil eyes, a row of small white fangs, and two short clawed forelimbs at the sides. The body is olive-khaki with blue-black spots and a pale grey-blue belly. East is a long, slim eel body seen in profile, with a small crocodilian head on the right, one small clawed forelimb under the neck, dark blue spots along the flank, a grey-blue belly band, and a tail that tapers to a thin point with no paddle. North is the back of a torpedo-shaped body, spotted, with the two forelimbs poking out near the top and the tail end toward the bottom. North shows no face. All three facings have clean alpha.
observed.south.png: A front view of a stocky olive-brown animal. The head is broad and short-snouted, and the face is crocodile-like, with nostrils on top, yellow slit-pupil eyes on raised brows, and small white fangs along a wide closed mouth that curves up slightly at the corners. The short, thick forelimbs end in dark curved claws. The belly is rounded and grey-blue. The back has blue spots and a faint teal-blue iridescent sheen. The whole shape reads as a fat, rounded mass about as wide as it is tall. There are no whiskers or barbels and no glowing nodules.
observed.east.png: A side profile facing right. The body is long, flat and eel-like, olive-khaki above and grey-blue below, with a single row of dark blue spots along the flank and a faint iridescent sheen along the back ridge. The head is crocodilian, with a long snout, an interlocking row of small white teeth and a yellow eye. One small clawed forelimb hangs behind the head. The tail tapers to a flat point with no paddle. The body is thin (about 98 px tall) compared with its length (about 490 px). There are no whiskers or lures and no glowing fringe.
observed.north.png: A rear view. The back is olive with an iridescent sheen and two rows of dark blue spots. The body narrows toward the bottom of the frame into a rounded blunt tail end. The two clawed forelimbs show at the upper sides, and the top of the head is hidden behind the back. There is no face and there are no eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom, the creature lies about 2.5 cells long beside a vanilla human of about 1 cell; it is a slim, low eel. At 32 px per cell it reads as a long, thin, khaki-and-blue streak, longer than the rat and the human.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult: a dark olive serpentine body with dense dark spots, a glowing cyan fringe and rows of teal nodules, a large paddle-shaped tail, big curved white fangs, long jointed arms with large dark talons, and small mandible tendrils at the mouth. South shows the adult coiled with an open jaw; east is a sinuous profile; north is the back with the paddle tail.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on: snout, both eyes and the teeth toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the spotted back and the tapering tail end, with no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: No facing is a rotated top-down view. North is a rear view at the game angle, like the adult sibling's north.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 233% height spread is mostly the pose (a long horizontal profile against foreshortened front and rear views). But the mass does not agree between facings: south is a stout body about 250 px wide with a head about 180 px wide, while east is a slim eel only about 60 px thick with a head about 70 px tall. South looks far heavier than the animal on east.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: East shows a long, thin eel, but south shows a round, toad-like lump with no hint of that long, thin body. Palette, spots, eye and claws agree across the facings.

SIGNATURE.seen: The croc head and the pair of clawed forelimbs behind the head are visible on all three facings, though the limbs are small, as suits a young animal.

ALIEN.seen: A croc-headed eel with clawed arms is not a single Earth species. A stranger would not name it simply as an eel.

DEPARTURES.seen: Clawed forelimbs: present (small). Whisker-like lures: absent on every facing, with no barbels or whiskers on the snout. Pale body: only partly present; the belly is pale grey-blue, but the back is olive-khaki, which matches the canon colour layout and the adult sibling.

CANON.seen: Body plan: croc head, eel body and clawed arms are present, but the flat paddle tail is absent (the tail tapers to a point). Colour layout: olive back, blue-black spots, grey-blue belly and yellow eye are present, but the glowing cyan fringe and the teal nodules are absent; the canon infant (canon_2) is a smooth torpedo, so this may be intentional for a young animal. Croc head with slit-pupil yellow eye: present; the fangs are small. Mandibles: absent. Realistic rendering: present. Negative: not a plain eel (it has the croc head and arms).

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with textured skin, soft lighting and no outlines. The south face is soft and rounded, with a mouth line that curves up slightly, which leans toward cute but stays within what a young animal may look like.

OURS.seen: The art matches the adult sibling's species design in our style. No vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-outs on all three facings, with no water, ground or shadow.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Young proportions (a larger head for the body on south, short limbs, soft features) are present, and the art reads as the same species as the adult by head, spots and claws, though it lacks the adult's glow and paddle tail.

SCALE.seen: About 2.5 cells long beside the human, smaller than the adult; plausible for a young animal of a 40 m species within game limits.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a long spotted khaki eel shape apart from the brown ground.

Dark blotchy spots cover the back, flanks and rump. North: the rear, with the rump, the tail hanging down the centre, the hind legs and something pendulous between the hind legs. No face is visible. observed.facings.png: Three facings on one scale. South is a shaggy brown bovine calf facing the camera, with two small branched antlers and visible ears, eyes and muzzle. East is a side profile looking right, with a stocky barrel body, short tail, a low shaggy head and a broad muzzle. East is noticeably smaller and lower than the other two facings: from antler tip to hoof it is about 335 px, against about 423 px on south and about 458 px on north. North shows the rear: shaggy rump, a short tufted tail hanging down and the back of the head with ears and antlers, with no face. North stands taller than south.
observed.south.png: Front view of a shaggy, light-to-mid brown calf. A long fringe of fur falls over half-closed eyes, the muzzle is broad and cow-like, and two short branched antlers (three tines each) rise from the crown. There are rounded ears, four legs with cloven hooves and a soft painterly fur texture. There is no outline, and the background is clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Right-facing profile of a stocky shaggy grazer. The head is held low, the muzzle is cow-like, branched antlers sit on the crown, the ear is rounded, the tail is a short tuft, the legs are fairly short and the hooves cloven. Soft realistic painterly fur, no keyline and no ground shadow.
observed.north.png: Rear view: a broad shaggy rump with a tufted tail hanging centred. The backs of the ears and two branched antlers show above the head, and there is no face or eyes. The legs end in cloven hooves. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate's east facing stands beside the vanilla human. The calf is about as long as 1.5 cells and its back is near the human's shoulder. At normal play (32 px/cell) it reads as a brown shaggy lump on brown dirt. Its colour is close to the ground's colour, so contrast is low, but the silhouette still separates from the ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult FeralNerf: a dark reddish-brown, heavily humped bison-like animal with grey-black CURVED horns (bison horns), a long thin tufted tail and dark hooves. The rendering is grittier and more contrasty, with dark edge pixels. The adult has no antlers.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face toward the camera: eyes under the fringe, muzzle, both antlers and ears symmetric.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the rump and the tufted tail, with the back of the head, ears and antlers. There are no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the angled game camera with the legs visible. None is a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: On the shared-scale panel east is clearly smaller: its body, head and antlers are all smaller, not just a shorter pose. North is taller than south. This agrees with the measured 34% spread (east 171 px vs north 230 px).

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same palette, fur and branched antlers appear on all three facings, and the antlers turn with the head (a symmetric pair on south and north, offset pair in profile on east).

SIGNATURE.seen: Stocky, antlered, low shaggy head, coarse brown fur: all visible and legible.

ALIEN.seen: At first glance this is a Highland cattle calf with deer antlers placed on its head. The cow muzzle, fringe and body are wholly bovine, and the antlers are the only non-Earth cue. That is the 'departures bolted on' case for earth_body_named: no.

DEPARTURES.seen: Line 1, 'antlers, not the curved horns of a bison': present. Branched antlers with about three tines each show on every facing.

STYLE.seen: Realistic painterly fur with no keyline, not cel-shaded and not a 3D render. The face is soft but not cartoonish or smiling.

OURS.seen: Not a vanilla or other-mod sprite. The art is fresh, with consistent artpipe output across the facings.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on all facings: no ground patch, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The note requires the young to 'read as the same species as the adult' with 'horns or crests small or budding'. The kept adult is a dark red-brown humped bison with curved black horns. The young is a lighter tan-brown Highland-calf shape with fully branched antlers, which are not budding and are a different headgear type from the adult's horns. Side by side, the two read as different animals.

SCALE.seen: The calf is smaller than the adult sibling and stands about shoulder-high to the human. That is plausible for an 18-day young of a large grazer.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it reads as a brown shaggy quadruped against the dirt. Contrast is low (brown on brown) but the silhouette holds.

concerns.evidence: Across the candidate facings, the animal has a relatively level back, short furry tail and conspicuous branched antlers. The sibling's east view has a pronounced shoulder hump, long thin tail and heavy curved horns. The candidate's shorter legs support a young appearance, but its appendages and body silhouette do not clearly connect it to that adult.

The individual candidate sprites have softly blended tan-brown fur and subdued contours. In siblings.png, the adult has saturated reddish-brown fur, sharply separated dark fur clumps and much stronger edge contrast. These differences remain apparent in the shared-scale presentations.

In facings.png, the east animal has a noticeably smaller head and shallower torso than the south animal, as well as shorter-looking legs. North is taller than south. The lowered east head explains some height difference, but the smaller body parts show that pose alone does not explain the measured 34% spread.

South shows a broad cattle muzzle beneath a shaggy forehead fringe, and east shows a familiar Highland-cattle body and head silhouette. The branched antlers are visible, satisfying the listed departure, but read as additions to that familiar bovine anatomy.

edits.change: The calf wears the adult's dark reddish-brown coat and carries the adult's humped shoulder line and long thin tail with a tufted tip. Its headgear is a pair of small budding antler knobs on the crown, each a short single spike angled up and back.

The calf is painted in the adult's deep red-brown palette. Its coarse fur is built from strongly separated clumps in dark red-brown, mid red-brown and a few warm highlights. The painted contrast and gritty texture match the adult, and only the proportions are younger.

The front view, the side view and the rear view show one calf at one body scale. Head size, torso volume, limb length and shoulder height are identical on every view. In the side view the head hangs low, at the same size as in the front view.

The head is low and heavy, with a broad flat squared grazing snout and wide nostrils. A heavy low-slung shaggy mane drapes over the hump and shoulders. The eyes sit visible under a coarse brow ridge. The body is a stocky, hump-shouldered grazer, longer in the rump than a barrel.

The calf's silhouette has the adult's shape in miniature: a raised shoulder hump, a sloping back, a long thin tufted tail, and budding antler knobs that prefigure the adult's headgear. The shoulder hump is clearly visible in the side view.
The fur-clump definition and the contrast match the adult sibling: deep reddish-brown with dark shadow gaps between clumps. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast carry the silhouette.

All three views are painted to one proportion chart for the calf: head length is a fixed share of body length, the limbs have the same length, and the rear view stands at the same height as the front view.

The calf carries the adult nerf's own proportions in a younger body: the same low shaggy head, the same flat broad snout, the same shoulder hump and the same mane. Species identity reads from the whole animal, and the antlers are one feature among many.

Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast carry the silhouette

Its coat is the same deep reddish-brown as the adult: coarse, gritty fur built from strongly separated clumps, in dark red-brown, mid red-brown and a few warm highlights, with dark shadow gaps between clumps and high painted contrast. The head is low and heavy, with a broad, flat, squared grazing snout and wide nostrils. The eyes sit visible under a coarse brow ridge. A heavy low-slung shaggy mane drapes over the hump and shoulders. On the crown sit two small budding antler knobs, each a short single spike angled up and back, which clearly prefigure the adult's full headgear. Younger proportions: slightly shorter legs and a slightly larger head than the adult, with the same hump, the same mane and the same tail. All three views show one calf at one body scale: identical head size, torso volume, limb length and shoulder height on every view; in the side view the head hangs low at the same size as in the front view. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast carry the silhouette against any ground.

observed.facings.png: Three facings of one uniformly warm brown-tan, barrel-bodied quadruped on a checkerboard. South (left) is a front view: the face looks at the camera, with two large upright pointed ears, small dark eyes, a pale snout that ends in a small blunt nub-horn, and four clawed feet. East (centre) is a true right-facing profile: a long level back, a short stub tail, short wrinkled legs with three or four claws, and a long drooping tapir-like snout with a thick lower lip and a small horn nub at the tip. North (right) is the rear: haunches, a stub tail and the backs of the ears, with no face. At the shared scale, east is clearly smaller than south and north. North is the tallest: its ears sit highest and its feet lowest.
observed.south.png: Front view. The head faces the camera. The ears are large and lighter inside. The eyes are small and dark, the muzzle is pale tan, and a small blunt pale horn nub sits at the tip of the snout. The body is a wide barrel with skin wrinkles at the legs. The feet are broad, with pale claws. The coat is uniform brown-tan with no stripes. The alpha is clean.
observed.east.png: Right-facing side profile. The body is long and low and the back is level. A stub tail points up at the rear. The legs are short and wrinkled, with three or four claws visible per foot. The snout is long and drooping, with a pale muzzle, a thick lower lip and a tiny horn nub. The ears are pointed and the eye is small and dark. The coat is smooth, short and uniform brown-tan, and the belly is slightly paler. The figure fills less of the canvas than south or north do. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: Rear view: a rounded rump, a short stub tail, the hind legs with wrinkles and claws, and the two ears visible over the back of the head. No eyes and no face. The coat is uniform brown-tan. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the young sits beside the vanilla human. The body is about one cell long and stands about as high as the human's torso. That is plausible for the young of a medium-sized animal. At 32 px per cell it is a small brown-tan shape on a brown-tan ground: the silhouette reads, but with low value contrast.
observed.siblings.png: The kept adult male mott. A sage-grey back and rump, orange-rust flanks and legs with cream horizontal bands, and a cream belly. The head is short and broad, rhino-hippo-like, with a prominent upturned horn on the nose. A thin dark edge runs around the silhouette.

reply.subject: RSW_Orray__young
reply.image_seen: Shared-scale facings and individual images show a grey-brown, pebbled quadruped with a broad frontal head, rounded belly, short clawed legs and intact tail; the scale panel shows it beside a human, and the sibling panel shows a warmer-brown adult.

concerns.evidence: East has a rounded, hanging belly, thick shoulders and substantial thighs on short legs. Those structures agree with the broad torso and powerful limbs in south and north. The conspicuous difference in apparent bulk is a facing-scale problem, confirmed under K2; the profile does not establish a separate slender body plan.

In the shared-scale panel, east's head, torso and legs are conspicuously smaller than their frontal and rear counterparts. The measured heights are 163 px east versus 336 px south and 376 px north. North's projecting tail contributes to its height, but does not explain the much larger head and limbs in south.
East visibly has a deep, convex belly between thick upper legs, a broad neck and heavy shoulders. Its low back does not make the torso slender; the required stout body is present.

The alligator resemblance is concentrated in the long muzzle and tapering tail, both consistent with the canon description. East also shows the required heavy belly, thick wrinkled grey-brown hide and stubby powerful legs. This is an RSW canon subject, for which the class module explicitly permits Earth-animal resemblance.

The young east view has a proportionally substantial head, shorter muzzle and shorter legs than the adult east reference. Both share a heavy belly, thick neck, clawed feet and pebbled hide. The adult's higher back and curled tail differ, but a matching hump or tail pose is not required for the young stage.

East shows four short, muscular legs supporting a low, rounded torso with a hanging belly. Its snout is elongated, eyes small and high, hide tuberculate, and tail intact. The claimed absence of a stout quadrupedal body is not supported by those visible features.

South's mouth corners curve upward, but the mouth remains a textured anatomical crease beneath the muzzle. Small recessed eyes, irregular leathery folds and restrained shading give the face a realistic reptilian treatment rather than a mascot or toy treatment.

The candidate is cooler grey-brown than the adult, but both use mottled earth colours, densely pebbled hide and similar painterly modelling. Grey-brown is explicitly permitted by the card. The adult's warmer muzzle does not establish a required marking for the young.

request.prompt: A young orray, a stout reptile from Geonosis, painted as a single sprite sheet of three facings of the SAME animal at ONE consistent scale: front view (south, eyes toward the viewer), rear view (north, seen from behind: back, haunches and tail, eyes hidden), and side profile (east, facing right). The orray is a heavy, low-slung, barrel-bodied reptile with thick grey-brown hide, a darker grey-brown back, a paler warm-grey belly, short powerful legs with broad clawed feet, and a long rooting snout with a blunt tip and small nostrils. It is a young animal, so its head and eye are slightly large for its compact body, and its snout is long and slightly shorter than an adult's. Thick hide with coarse, wrinkled, pebbled texture and heavy folds at the neck and shoulders. The tail is short and thick. Consistent size across all three facings: the shoulder height above the ground is the same in the front, rear and side views; the torso depth in the side view equals the torso width in the front and rear views; head size, snout length, leg length and foot size are identical in each view; all three animals fill the same frame height and carry the same bulk. Natural foreshortening is the only difference: the snout points toward the viewer in the front view, and the tail points toward the viewer in the rear view. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld style, top-lit with gentle shading under the belly, transparent background.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard: a stocky, bare-skinned, wrinkled taupe-brown quadruped with a large splayed fan of long cream-tipped quills over the back, rump and flanks. South shows the face head-on, with one large eye in the middle of the forehead and a hooked, beak-like snout with small fangs at its sides. East shows a side profile walking right, with a long curved hooked snout, fangs, one eye high on the side of the head, quills sweeping back to a pointed tail, a paler bare belly and clawed feet. North shows the rear: a quill mass, a stubby tail nub, haunches and the soles of the hind feet, and no face. All three are drawn at similar sizes.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution: a single round brown eye centred on the forehead above a down-hooked snout with two small fangs. The quill fan rises behind the head like a mane. Thick wrinkled forelegs with heavy claws. The paler wrinkled chest and belly are bare. Painterly shading with no outline, on clean alpha.
observed.east.png: True right-facing profile. Barrel body, short thick legs, and a large hooked snout with a curved tip and fangs. One dark eye sits high on the side of the head near the brow. Long straight quills run from the nape over the back and down the flanks to a pointed tail. The belly is bare and paler. Clean alpha with no ground shadow.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The quill mass covers the back and rump, and a short tapering tail hangs down the middle. The hind legs and feet are seen from behind. No eyes and no face. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the animal is roughly as long as the human is tall and a little shorter than the human. At 32 px per cell it reads as a spiky grey-brown lump beside the human and the rat. The quill silhouette is distinct, but the brown body has only moderate contrast with the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult (reference) is drawn in greyscale with ink hatching and dark keylines. The adult stands upright on its hind legs, with a strongly pale belly, a single forehead eye, quills that also frame the head, a gaping fanged hooked mouth and long claws. It looks more ferocious and more stylised than the candidate.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the quill-covered back, the tail nub and the hind feet. No face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All facings are drawn from the oblique game camera. None is a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 9%, and the facings look matched in the shared-scale panel.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same hide, palette, quill fan and claws appear on every facing, and the quills turn with the body. Minor point: on east the single eye sits where a normal side eye would, not visibly on the forehead midline.

SIGNATURE.seen: The single forehead eye is clear on south, and the long quills along the spine and flanks dominate every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The quills suggest a porcupine, but the bare wrinkled hide, the cyclopean eye, the hooked fanged snout and the heavy clawed rhino-like legs keep it from reading as an Earth animal.

request.prompt:
A juvenile skalder, a heavy grey-green herbivore from the volcanic world Florrum, drawn as a single RimWorld creature sprite on a transparent background. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. The whole animal is visible and fills the frame with a small margin.

Body: a heavy, barrel-bodied quadruped with thick, leathery grey-green hide, a deep chest, a broad back and short sturdy legs. It is a young animal, so the head is broader and rounder, the features are softer, the legs are shorter and the proportions are stockier than an adult's. The hide is mottled grey-green with matte, slightly rough texture.

Mantle: the signature feature, built exactly like the adult skalder's. A few broad, smooth, ridged plates, about three to five, arch over the neck and shoulders in one sweeping curve. They hood the neck and frame the head, then taper along the upper back. Each plate has a gently ridged surface and a rounded edge, and the plates overlap like a heavy protective collar. The mantle is a darker, slightly olive grey-green than the body. It is smaller than the adult's in absolute size but still huge compared with the juvenile's body.

Stripes: bold vertical pale stripes, cream-grey against the grey-green hide, run down the broad flanks. They are the same stripe pattern as the adult, in a smaller juvenile scale.

Head and tusks: a broad, rounded head with a blunt muzzle, small dark eyes and softly rounded features. Two short, stubby ivory tusks curve slightly out and down from the lower jaw. The mantle's front plates arch over the back of the head.

Palette: grey-green hide, darker olive-grey mantle plates, pale cream-grey stripes, warm ivory tusks, dark grey hooves. Lighting is soft and even, from the upper left, in the vanilla RimWorld painterly manner.

The disc is low and flat, with its height a small fraction of its width, and the whole rim meets the ground all the way round, so the body hugs the ground like a fitted lid and the underside stays hidden. A few small, dull, matte red eyes and a thin, neutral mouth slit are sunk into the rim, spaced along its edge. Facings: south view, front rim toward the viewer, with the eyes and mouth slit along the near edge. East view, side-on, the same flat disc seen from its side with the low ruffled profile and a few eyes along the near rim. North view, rear rim toward the viewer, the smooth mottled back of the mantle with its ruffled edge and the eyes hidden on the far side. All three facings share the same body size: the disc has the same width and the same height in each view and fills the same footprint on its canvas. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic rendering, transparent background, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.
